subject: general
question:
Identify the vegetative part and the reproductive part in the following diagram of Rhizopus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/29079ea2c96534535fdcc38dc5b38704e5121dc7faa224f678d059d25f1847ad.png]

options.text: Both a and b are vegetative parts
a is the reproductive part, whereas b is the vegetative part
Both a and b are reproductive parts
a is the vegetative part, whereas b is the reproductive part

solution:
The correct answer is __**a is the reproductive part, whereas b is the vegetative part**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **a** represents the **sporangium**, which is the **reproductive structure **in Rhizopus.
 
• The sporangium contains spores, which are released for reproduction.
 
• **b** represents the **hyphae**, which are the **vegetative parts **of Rhizopus.
 
• Hyphae are responsible for nutrient absorption and growth of the fungus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rhizopus**

 
 
• Rhizopus is a genus of common fungi that grows on organic substances like bread, fruits, and vegetables.
 
• They are known for their fast-growing nature and are often referred to as bread molds.
 
• Rhizopus species play a significant role in decomposition and nutrient cycling in ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Sporangium**
 
 
• The sporangium is a structure found in fungi, algae, and some plants, which produces and contains spores.
 
• In Rhizopus, the sporangium is the reproductive organ that releases spores to propagate the fungus.
 
 
 
• **Hyphae**
 
 
• Hyphae are the long, thread-like structures that make up the body of a fungus.
 
• They form a network called mycelium, which is involved in nutrient absorption and growth.
 
 
 
• **Spores**
 
 
• Spores are reproductive units in fungi, capable of developing into a new individual without sexual fusion.
 
• They are usually resistant to adverse environmental conditions and can remain dormant until conditions are favorable for growth.
